benchmarks.title: Tokyo Skytree: 450 m redshift with transportable optical lattice clocks
benchmarks.citation: Takamoto, M. et al. Test of general relativity by a pair of transportable optical lattice clocks. Nature Photonics 14, 411–415 (2020); numbers as summarized by Shinkai, Takamoto & Katori, arXiv:2502.06104 (2025).
benchmarks.what_is_checked: The engine's WGS84 normal-field potential difference for the clocks' laser-ranged height difference, against the redshift the clocks measured and the geodetic value.

rows.note: The paper uses measured local gravity 9.797248 m/s²; the engine uses WGS84 normal gravity (9.797232 m/s² at mid-height), which here happens to agree to well within 10⁻¹⁸.

benchmarks.title: Fréjus tunnel (Modane) to Torino: first chronometric levelling with a transportable clock
benchmarks.citation: Grotti, J. et al. Geodesy and metrology with a transportable optical clock. Nature Physics 14, 437–441 (2018); arXiv:1705.04089.
benchmarks.what_is_checked: The engine's redshift relation and Sr reference frequency, converting the measured 47.92(83) Hz shift to a potential difference, against the paper's clock value and the independent geodetic determination.

rows.quantity: Potential difference ΔΦ vs paper's clock value
rows.criterion: within ±0.5 m²/s² (rounding of the published value)
within ±0.5 m²/s² (rounding of the published value)

rows.note: Geodetic value 10 032.1(16) m²/s² from GNSS, levelling and a refined geoid model.

benchmarks.title: Buried sphere detectable by clocks (synthetic case)
benchmarks.citation: Bondarescu, R. et al. Geophysical applicability of atomic clocks: direct continental geoid mapping. Geophysical Journal International 191, 78–82 (2012); arXiv:1209.2889.
benchmarks.what_is_checked: The engine's sphere potential and gravity for a 1.5 km radius sphere with 20 % density contrast (534 kg/m³) centred 2 km deep, and the minimum-radius relation.

rows.criterion: within ±0.005 m²/s² (rounding of the published value)
within ±0.05 mGal (rounding of the published value)

rows.quantity: Smallest detectable radius at 45 km (ΔU = 0.2 m²/s²)
rows.criterion: within ±0.5 km (rounding of the published value)
rows.note: Published as “a sphere of 4 km radius … down to 45 km depth”.
g·Δh/c² ≈ 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁸ per cm (also stated by Shinkai, Takamoto & Katori 2025).

method: Published values recomputed with the engine's physics functions; no parameter is fitted.
